map.name: Inbox Helper
map.summary: An AI email assistant that syncs a user's Gmail, summarizes threads and can send replies on their behalf.

nodes.label: Email senders
nodes.evidence: Anyone can email a user, so message bodies are untrusted.
how: Anyone on the internet can send mail to a user, so every message body is untrusted input

nodes.label: Gmail API
nodes.evidence: polls the Gmail API every two minutes
how: Google OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow issues each user a long-lived refresh token
The Gmail API `users.history.list` returns changes since the last `historyId`
`send_email` goes out through the same Gmail API as the user

nodes.label: OpenAI API
how: Chat completions with tool calling on `gpt-4o`
Receives the full thread, earlier mail and the tool results in each prompt

nodes.label: Any website
nodes.evidence: fetch_url makes an outbound HTTP request to any URL
how: Any URL found in an email; `fetch_url` requests it with `httpx` and follows redirects

nodes.label: Log service
nodes.evidence: Logs go to Better Stack, including full agent prompts
how: `logtail-python` ships every agent prompt and reply to Better Stack for debugging

nodes.label: Web app
how: React single page app; Google sign-in through `@react-oauth/google`
Renders summaries and drafts from Markdown with `react-markdown`
Calls the API with the session cookie

nodes.label: API
how: FastAPI on Fly.io; `google_callback` swaps the Google code for tokens with `google-auth-oauthlib`
Keeps sessions in a signed cookie, and the /admin dashboard trusts the same cookie plus an `is_admin` flag
Encrypts refresh tokens with Fernet (AES-128-CBC with HMAC-SHA256) under `TOKEN_KEY` before saving them

nodes.label: Mail sync worker
nodes.evidence: polls the Gmail API every two minutes with each user's OAuth refresh token
how: `poll_inbox` runs on an APScheduler interval of 120 seconds for every user
Decrypts each refresh token and calls Gmail `users.history.list` since the last `historyId`
Saves new messages to Postgres, then enqueues `triage_thread` on Redis with RQ

nodes.label: Triage agent
nodes.evidence: can call tools: send_email, fetch_url, search_mail
how: `triage_thread` loads the thread and the 20 most recent related messages from Postgres
Runs an OpenAI tool-calling loop on `gpt-4o` for up to 5 steps
Tools: `send_email`, `fetch_url` with `httpx`, and `search_mail` with Postgres full-text search
Auto-sends replies under 50 words without asking the user

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.evidence: OAuth refresh tokens (encrypted ...), message bodies and summaries
how: Supabase Postgres: users, message bodies, summaries and refresh tokens
Refresh tokens are Fernet ciphertext; the key is `TOKEN_KEY` in the environment
`search_mail` queries message bodies with Postgres full-text search

nodes.label: Job queue
nodes.evidence: the job queue between the sync worker and the agent
how: Redis list used by RQ; each job carries a thread id to triage

assumptions: Google sign in is the only way to log in.
The agent uses the same Gmail scopes as the sync worker, including send.
Fly.io and Supabase are one trust zone, because the API and the workers share database credentials.
The web app renders Markdown without stripping images or links.

analysis.verdict: Fix the triage agent first: any email can make it forward private mail or fetch an attacker's URL, so turn off auto-send and fence its tools. Then stop sending full prompts to the log service.

threats.title: A malicious email takes over the triage agent
threats.summary: Anyone can email a user instructions that the agent follows, such as forwarding private mail to the sender.
threats.statement: An outside sender who can email any user can hide instructions in a message that the triage agent reads and follows, which leads to the agent calling send_email to forward private mail to the sender, resulting in reduced confidentiality of users' inboxes.
threats.impact: Private mail leaks from every account that receives the email, without anyone clicking anything.
fixes: Turn off auto-send and require the user to approve every send_email call
Allow send_email only to addresses already in the thread
threats.evidence: Auto-send is on by default for replies under 50 words, and anyone can email a user.

threats.title: fetch_url carries mail out in a link
threats.summary: Injected instructions can make the agent fetch an attacker's URL with private mail in the query string.
threats.statement: An outside sender whose email reaches the triage agent can instruct it to call fetch_url on an attacker's URL with summaries appended, which leads to private mail reaching the attacker's server, resulting in reduced confidentiality of users' inboxes.
threats.impact: Mail leaks even with auto-send off, because fetching a link looks harmless.
fixes: Fetch only URLs that appear in the original email, never ones the model builds
Route fetches through a proxy that blocks private addresses and strips query strings
threats.evidence: fetch_url makes an outbound HTTP request to any URL found in an email.

threats.title: Full prompts put private mail in the logs
threats.summary: Every email the agent reads is copied into the log service, where more people can read it.
threats.statement: Anyone with access to the log service can read full agent prompts, which leads to private email bodies being exposed outside the database's access controls, resulting in reduced confidentiality of users' inboxes.
threats.impact: A leaked log token or an over-shared dashboard exposes mail from every user.
fixes: Log prompt ids, token counts and tool names, not prompt text
Set a short retention period on the log service
threats.evidence: Logs go to Better Stack, including full agent prompts for debugging.

threats.title: Admin pages trust the ordinary session
threats.summary: One admin route that forgets the is_admin check gives any signed-in user admin powers.
threats.statement: A signed-in user who finds an /admin route without the is_admin check can call it with their normal session cookie, which leads to reading or changing any user's account, resulting in reduced confidentiality and integrity of every account.
threats.impact: A single missed check turns any account into an administrator.
fixes: Guard every /admin route with one deny-by-default middleware
Give the admin dashboard its own sign in with MFA
threats.evidence: The admin dashboard at /admin uses the same session cookie, guarded by an is_admin flag.

threats.title: Markdown images leak summaries
threats.summary: A summary that contains an image link makes the browser send data to the attacker's server.
threats.statement: An outside sender who can steer a summary can make it include a Markdown image whose URL carries private text, which leads to the user's browser sending that text to the attacker when the summary renders, resulting in reduced confidentiality of users' mail.
threats.impact: Mail leaks silently whenever a user opens a summary.
fixes: Render summaries without images, or proxy images through an allowlist
Set a Content-Security-Policy that blocks images from other origins
threats.evidence: The web app shows summaries and drafts rendered as Markdown.

threats.title: One env key unlocks every Gmail token
threats.summary: Whoever reads the database and the environment gets access to every user's Gmail.
threats.statement: An attacker who obtains a database dump and the environment variable key can decrypt every refresh token, which leads to full Gmail access for every user, resulting in reduced confidentiality of all connected inboxes.
threats.impact: One leaked backup plus one leaked secret exposes every connected mailbox.
fixes: Encrypt refresh tokens with a key held in a KMS, not an environment variable
Request the narrowest Gmail scopes, and split read and send into separate grants
threats.evidence: OAuth refresh tokens (encrypted with a key from an environment variable)

threats.title: Email floods run up the model bill
threats.summary: Anyone can send thousands of emails, and each one triggers a paid model call.
threats.statement: An outside sender who can email a user in bulk can trigger a triage job per message, which leads to thousands of OpenAI calls and exhausted quotas, resulting in reduced availability of triage for every user.
threats.impact: A cheap email flood becomes an expensive outage.
fixes: Cap model calls per user per day and skip bulk or list mail
Batch several new messages into one triage call
threats.evidence: For each new thread it reads the messages and earlier mail.

paths.title: Poisoned email forwards the inbox
paths.story: An attacker emails the user a message with hidden instructions. During triage the agent follows them and uses send_email to forward private mail to the attacker.

paths.title: Poisoned email leaks mail through a link
paths.story: The same hidden instructions tell the agent to fetch an attacker's URL with summaries in the query string, so private mail leaves even with auto-send off.

paths.title: Any account reaches the admin pages
paths.story: A signed-in user calls an admin route that forgot the is_admin check and reads other users' accounts straight from Postgres.

What happens if an email tells the agent.answer: The email reaches the Triage agent through the Gmail API, the sync worker and Postgres, and the agent can follow its instructions with send_email (T1), or leak mail through fetch_url (T2). Turning off auto-send and limiting send_email to addresses in the thread breaks the first route.

What should I fix first, and why?.answer: Fix the Triage agent first (T1): it reads private mail, takes instructions from anyone who emails the user, and can send data out with send_email and fetch_url, so one email can make it forward or leak a user's mail (T2). Turn off auto-send, allow send_email only to addresses already in the thread, and fetch only URLs from the original email. Then stop sending full prompts to the Log service (T3).

What can untrusted input make Triage age.answer: Anyone can email a user, and the message reaches the Triage agent through the Gmail API, the sync worker and Postgres, so the sender's words steer an agent that holds tools. They can make it forward private mail with send_email (T1), put mail in an attacker's URL with fetch_url (T2), or write a summary with an image link that leaks it from the Web app (T5).

What happens if Postgres leaks?.answer: Postgres holds every user's message bodies, summaries and Gmail refresh tokens, so a leak exposes all of that mail at once. The tokens are encrypted with one key from the environment, so whoever also gets that key can read and send mail as every user (T6). Keep the key in a KMS instead, and ask Gmail for the narrowest scopes.
